newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends up sharply as cash steadies.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends up sharply as cash steadies.

text.p: Reports that cash lumber has steadied and may have reached a bottom continued to prompt demand in CME lumber futures and prices ended sharply higher for the fourth consecutive day, traders said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce down another $1.00 per tbf at $366.00, but the decline was slowing and there were increased reports of spruce selling in the $360 to $370 area. Cash prices have tumbled $66 since the recent high set September 13 and wholesaler interest was developing.
Traders also cited the higher bond prices and lower interest rates as constructive. Lower interest rates should boost home sales, they said.

Buying demand was uneven ahead of the weekend with the market now looking technically stronger after breaking through congestion on the charts. November should go up to fill the gap in the charts at $361, they added.
Lumber closed $7.60 to $0.90 higher with November up $7.40 at $358.40 and January up most at $369.60 per tbf.
